bibliographic.title: Ethical perspectives on deployment of large language model agents in biomedicine: a survey
bibliographic.authors: Nafiseh Ghaffar Nia; Amin Amiri; Yuan Luo; Adrienne Kline
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ghaffar Nia, N., Amiri, A., Luo, Y., & Kline, A. (2026). Ethical perspectives on deployment of large language model agents in biomedicine: a survey. AI and Ethics, 6, 32. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43681-025-00847-w

methodology.sample_description: peer-reviewed literature on the ethical dimensions of LLMs and LLM-based agents across technical, biomedical, and societal domains
methodology.technology_context: large language models; LLM-based agents; agentic and embodied systems

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed survey on ethical deployment of LLM agents in biomedicine, mapping risks, mitigation strategies, and governance frameworks relevant to regulated use. It strongly addresses LLMs, accountability, guardrailing, and post-deployment monitoring, but the provided text does not establish conversational systems, chatbots, or conversational governance as the primary object of study.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and abstract-level text were provided; full review methods, search strategy, inclusion criteria, and conversational/agent interaction coverage require manual verification.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is limited to page 1/front matter. The study clearly states it conducts a review and synthesizes risks and mitigation strategies, but reporting details on search, selection, appraisal of included studies, and analytic procedure are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The abstract presents a coherent ethical and governance-oriented synthesis for LLM agents in biomedicine, but the available excerpt does not document review methods or empirical depth sufficiently to support high confidence in methodological adequacy.

coding.theme: Ethical and governance dimensions of LLM agent deployment in biomedicine
coding.subtheme: Risk mitigation, accountability, and monitoring for trustworthy LLM systems
rq_alignment: risk and compliance in regulated healthcare

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs and LLM-based agents introduce significant ethical risks in biomedicine, and trustworthy deployment requires technical reliability, transparency, accountability, mitigation strategies, and stronger governance practices.
synthesis.contribution: Maps ethical risks across technical, biomedical, and societal domains; distills mitigation strategies such as evaluation, red-teaming, alignment, guardrailing, privacy-preserving practices, and bias reduction; and examines governance frameworks while identifying gaps in context-aware evaluation, reporting standards, and post-deployment monitoring.
synthesis.limitations: Based on the provided excerpt, detailed review methodology, sample size, and conversational-governance specificity are unclear; the authors also note persistent gaps including limited context-aware evaluation, uneven reporting standards, and weak post-deployment monitoring.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for ethical risk taxonomy, governance frameworks, guardrails, accountability, and post-deployment monitoring gaps in regulated biomedical LLM/agent deployment; not sufficient on its own as central evidence for conversational governance without full-text confirmation.
